title: Sparse genotypes and Firth correction

blocks.what_we_do: Compare an explicitly forced Firth fit at a low-frequency retained autosomal site.
blocks.why: Rare genotypes can have very few case or control observations. Ordinary logistic fitting uses maximum likelihood: it chooses coefficients that make the observed outcomes most plausible under the model. If a predictor separates outcomes completely, that coefficient can diverge. Firth penalisation reduces small-sample bias and can give finite estimates. It does not create information or fix confounding, miscalled genotypes or a poor study design. The main scan in this dataset did not actually require Firth fallback; we force it for a transparent teaching comparison at one retained low-frequency site. Sites below the 1% main-path filter are not reintroduced.
blocks.you_need: The final cohort, main results and covariates from 6.3.
blocks.command:
```{r s6-6}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
minor <- pmin(results$A1_FREQ, 1 - results$A1_FREQ)
candidates <- which(results$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22) & valid_p(results$P) & minor > 0)
chosen <- results$ID[candidates[which.min(minor[candidates])]]
guided_list(chosen, guided_path(cfg, "6.6", "variant.txt"))
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), "--snp", chosen, "--covar", guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"),
  "--covar-name", "Age,PC1-PC10", "--covar-variance-standardize", "--glm", "firth", "sex", "hide-covar", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "6.6", "firth")))
comparison <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.6", "firth"))
print(results[results$ID == chosen, c("ID", "A1", "OR", "P")])
print(comparison[, c("ID", "A1", "OR", "P")])
stopifnot(nrow(comparison) == 1L, valid_p(comparison$P))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s5-7_state --extract results/guided/s6-6_variant.txt --covar results/guided/s6-3_covariates.tsv --covar-name Age,PC1-PC10 --covar-variance-standardize --glm firth sex hide-covar --out results/guided/s6-6_firth --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The R command uses `--snp` with the selected ID; the equivalent terminal command uses `--extract` with its one-ID file. `--glm firth` requests Firth for that variant rather than waiting for fallback. Other covariate and resource options match 6.4. `--pfile` reads the final genotype state; `--out` sets the report prefix. `--threads 2` limits worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the workspace budget in MiB.
blocks.expected_result:
One finite forced-Firth result, compared with the ordinary main-scan estimate for the same A1 allele. Small numerical differences are expected; forced Firth is not a new preferred genome-wide scan.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks passed on Windows; main test counts and significance match the instructor reference.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Does using Firth make an association based on very few carriers precise?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. It can stabilise fitting while uncertainty remains large.

</details>
blocks.files_created: Selected variant ID, the forced-Firth report and logs.
